item.title: Florida oyster reef restoration helped marine life return within 18 months
item.description: In Florida's Indian River Lagoon, restored oyster reefs have sparked impressive marine life revitalization. Species diversity reached parity with that of thriving reefs in a mere year, while overall invertebrate abundance required eighteen months for similar recovery. Notably, flatback mud crab populations surged alongside developments in reef structures and oyster density, highlighting how environmental factors shape the resurgence of these marine communities. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Study finds violence affects millions across US with links to health, economic hardship
item.description: A new national study reveals the widespread reach of violence across the United States, finding that more than half of U.S. adults have experienced physical violence and nearly half have experienced sexual violence in their lifetimes. The U.S. National Study on Violence Experiences Across the Lifespan (USVEX) also shows stark disparities in who experiences violence and how closely violence is linked to economic hardship, mental health and substance use. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Tracking the path of new world screwworm
item.description: New cases of New World screwworm have recently surfaced in the United States, highlighting the critical need to track its paths to determine where future infestations may occur. Researchers at the U.S. Department of Agriculture's (USDA) Agricultural Research Service (ARS) are employing predictive models as part of a forward-thinking approach to manage New World screwworm.
